title: A four-orbit K2-22 depth peak does not pass a ten-lag shuffle test in Campaign 1
abstract: We test the exploratory four-orbit depth correlation of the known dust-emitting planet K2-22b. Two reductions of 3274 common K2 exposures give 102 accepted orbits and 45 lag-four pairs. The correlations are 0.244 and 0.207. Shuffles within ten-orbit bins give tail fractions of 0.356 and 0.434 for the largest positive correlation across lags one to ten. Quadratic baselines also fail this search test at 0.05. A wider baseline gives a three-orbit peak, but it weakens on the original orbit set. A constant triangular transit at the actual exposure times gives lag-four correlation -0.040. This simple sampling model does not explain the positive peak. The results do not establish dust memory or exclude weak physical correlation. Both reductions share exposures. No new planet or independent telescope confirmation is found. Code, aggregate results, source hashes and separate-scratch retrieval steps support reproduction.

display.caption: Depth correlation across lags one to ten for four measurement choices. The dashed curve is a fixed triangular transit sampled at the actual exposure times. Both reductions share exposures.

citations.reason: Motivates a corrected test of its exploratory lag-four peak. No code or extracted records are reused.
Tests different, longer depth-modulation periods with the same archive inputs.
